blocks.text: Here are two reference screenshots of a revenue-recognition grid - they're the left and right halves of one wide table, panned sideways. Build a grid demo from them. Keep the design compact and minimalistic, and leave out the 'Columns' control panel docked on the right edge.

The two screenshots are one wide grid, panned - the right image is the left one scrolled sideways (the $1,941.67 Balance for "Dharma Initiative" lines up in both). Here's the aspect inventory I stitched together from them:

rows: Shape
A grouped tree on the row side plus two-level column headers on top
Rows

One indented Name column, 3 levels: Company (Dharma Initiative) > Contract (I-831, I-117, ...) > line item (Large - Access, Enterprise - Storage, ...), with expand/collapse chevrons and subtotal group rows
Columns
Total Amount (sorted descending) . Deferred Revenue . Recognized Revenue . Recognized %, then December 2024 and November 2024, each spanning a Balance and a Revenue column
Formatting
US currency like $1,234.56; a zero value renders as an em-dash placeholder; numbers right-aligned
Encodings
Recognized %: a muted "100%" label over a green progress bar; group rows bold and dark, leaf rows lighter
Pinned
The Name column stays put when the table scrolls right (a pinned row-facet column)
Excluded
The right-edge "Columns" control panel, per your request; compact, minimal chrome throughout
Domain
A SaaS revenue-recognition schedule: Company to Contract to line item, deferred vs recognized revenue with a monthly Balance/Revenue schedule

blocks.text: A few things the screenshots can't answer - my best guess is preselected in each:

items.question: Build it as a grouped tree table, or a true pivot?
items.answer: Grouped tree - one indented Name column with subtotal rows and grouped month headers (a true pivot would split Company/Contract/line into three stacked columns and lose the indented look)

items.question: Which interactions should actually work in the demo?
items.answer: Expand/collapse the tree, click-to-sort columns, and column resize

items.question: How much data should it generate, and what domain?
items.answer: Several companies (Dharma Initiative first), SaaS revenue recognition

blocks.text: Confirmed: grouped tree, with expand/collapse + click-to-sort + column resize, over several companies. Here's how each aspect maps to a grid mechanism before I build:

rows: Grouped 3-level tree
FlattenedDataViewModel + the flat layout; one persistent viewmodel, updateData() on every change; depth/leaf/expanded packed via createRowMeta
Pinned Name column
Native row-facet (the left region stays put on horizontal scroll)
Subtotal rows
Company/Contract rows carry summed measures; Recognized % is sum(Recognized) / sum(Total)
Two-level month headers
Two columnFacets levels; the month name spans its Balance/Revenue pair
Header + sort
One header renderer keyed by each column's unique value; default sort is Total Amount descending, matching the reference
Expand/collapse
A single delegated pointerdown on the mount recomputes the visible rows, then updateData() and redraw
Currency + em-dash
Intl.NumberFormat USD; a dash placeholder when a value is 0
Recognized % bar
A custom cell: a muted NN% label over a green progress track
Column resize
enableResizeUI, with clamped-width sizing that keeps the horizontal-scroll path
Theme
Matches the built-in light look, so it syncs the built-in light/dark pair with the page theme

blocks.text: Built it as packages/samples/src/demos/revenue-recognition. A compact grouped-tree table: a pinned Name column with a collapsible Company > Contract > line-item tree and subtotal rows; a two-level column band (four flat measures, then December and November 2024 each over Balance + Revenue); USD formatting with a dash for zeros; and a green inline recognition bar. Expand/collapse, click-to-sort (default Total Amount descending) and column resize all work, over one persistent viewmodel updated via updateData(). The theme follows the page light/dark.

Three deliberate deviations from the screenshots: several companies instead of only Dharma (Dharma is scaled largest so it still leads under the default sort); Recognized % varies - a mix of 100% and partials - so the bars and the Deferred column actually show range; and all numeric columns are right-aligned.
Did you only generate data for December and November 2024?

Yes - the per-row measures were only Total Amount, Deferred, and Recognized, plus a Balance and Revenue for December 2024 and November 2024. Those two month-groups were hardcoded, so the schedule stopped at November. I can make the months data-driven instead: generate N months of { balance, revenue } per line item and emit a column group per month, which also makes the horizontal scroll more meaningful. Want me to extend it?
Yes, extend the monthly schedule back through January.

Done - the schedule is now data-driven and runs December 2024 back to January 2024 (12 month-groups, each with a Balance and a Revenue column). Everything derives from a single MONTHS array, so the columns, headers, generator and subtotals all follow it; each line item generates a { balance, revenue } per month, and every group row sums them. Sorting works on any month column, and expand/collapse is unchanged.
With 12 months the table is now far wider than its container, so there's plenty of horizontal scroll with the Name column pinned.
